questions.q: A crystalline hydrated salt on being heated loses 45.6% of its weight. Percentage composition of anhydrous salt is Al - 10.5 %, K - 15.1 %, S - 24.8 %, O - 49.6 %. Find molecular formula of salt (hydrated) (M = 948 g/mol for hydrated salt).
questions.solution:
For anhydrous salt

$\begin{cases}\text{Element} & & \text{Al} & & \text{K} & & \text{S} & & \text{O} \\ \text{Atomic ratio} & & \dfrac{1 0 \cdot 5}{2 7} & & \dfrac{1 5 \cdot 1}{3 9} & & \dfrac{2 4 \cdot 8}{3 2} & & \dfrac{4 9 \cdot 6}{1 6} \\ & & 0 \cdot 3 9 & & 0 \cdot 3 9 & & 0 \cdot 7 8 & & 3 \cdot 1 0\end{cases}$

Empirical formula of anhydrous salt = KAlS2O8

E.F mass of Anhydrous salt = 258 g/mol

Mass of Moisture $= 2 5 8 \times \dfrac{4 5 \cdot 6}{5 4 \cdot 4} = 2 1 6 \text{g}$

$= \dfrac{2 1 6}{1 8} \approx 1 2 \text{mole}$

Empirical formula of Anhydrous salt KAlS2O8.12H2O

$\text{E F} \text{Mass} = 2 5 8 + 2 1 6 = 4 7 4$ g/Empirical formula mass

$\text{n} = \dfrac{\text{Mole Mass}}{\text{E.F. Mass}} = \dfrac{9 4 8}{4 7 4} = 2$

Molecular Formula = K2Al2S4O16.24H2O

= K2SO4.Al2(SO4)3.24H2O

mole of H2O2 used in first reaction

$= 17.5$

${wt. of HAsO}_{2} in sample$

$= \dfrac{\text{17.5}}{2} × \left(1 0 8\right) × 1 {0}^{- 3} = \text{0.945 g}$

${% of HAsO}_{2} \text{in the sample} = \dfrac{\text{0.945}}{\text{3.78}} × 1 0 0$

$= 25%$

questions.q: $0 . 63g$ of Oxalic acid is dissolved in order to obtain $250{cm}^{3}$ of its solution. Find the normality of this solution. [Oxalic acid:  \left( COOH{)}_{2} \cdot 2{H}_{2}O\right]$
questions.solution:
Molar mass of oxalic acid =& $126g / mol$

Mole =$\dfrac{Givenmass}{Molarmass} = \dfrac{0 . 63}{126} = 0 . 005mol$

Molarity =~$\dfrac{Moleofsolute}{Volumeofsolutioninml} \times 1000 = \dfrac{0 . 005}{250} \times 1000 = 0 . 02M$

Equivalent mass of oxalic acid =~$\dfrac{126}{2} = 63$

Gram equivalent of the solute =~$\dfrac{0 . 63}{63} = 0 . 01$

$Normality = \dfrac{Gramequivalentofsolute}{Volumeofsolutioninml} \times 1000 = \dfrac{0 . 01}{250} \times 1000 = 0 . 04N$

Hence, normality of solution is~$0 . 04N$.

questions.q: Gaseous benzene reacts with hydrogen gas in the presence of nickel catalyst to give gaseous cyclohexane. A mixture of benzene vapour and hydrogen had a pressure of 60 mm Hg in vessel. After all benzene converted to cyclohexane, the pressure of the gas was 30 mm Hg in the same volume and at the same temperature. What fraction (by mole) of the original mixture was benzene?
questions.solution:
${C}_{6}{H}_{6} \left(g\right) + 3{H}_{2} \left($g\right) \to ${C}_{6}{H}_{12}\left($g\right)$

Let x and y be the partial pressures (initial) of gaseous benzene and hydrogen in the vessel.

Then, \text{x} + \text{y} =$6 0$ ......... (i)

After the reaction, whole of benzene is converted to cyclohexane.

Partial pressure of cyclohexane $= x mm Hg$

Partial pressure of hydrogen left unreacted $= $\text{y} -$3 $\text{x}

Total pressure of the system after the reaction,

\text{x} + \text{y} -$3 $\text{x} = \text{y} -$2 $\text{x} =$3 0$ .......... (ii)

Solving (i) and (ii), \text{x} =$10 mm Hg$

Number of moles $∝$ pressure ; Volume $∝$ number of moles

Hence, fraction of benzene by volume in the original mixture $= $\dfrac{1 0}{6 0} = \dfrac{1}{6} = \text{0.167}$

questions.q:
In a certain operation,& $358g$ of ${TiCl}_{4}$~reacts with $96g$ of $Mg$. Calculate the yield of $Ti$ if $32g$ of $Ti$ is actually obtained [atomic weight of~$Ti= 48$, atomic weight of~$Mg= 24$]
&
questions.solution:
Balanced equation :

${TiCl}_{4} + 2Mg \to Ti + 2{MgCl}_{2}$

~Initial moles of~${TiCl}_{4}$~$= \dfrac{mass}{molarmass} = \dfrac{358}{190} = 1 . 88$

Initial moles of $Mg = \dfrac{96}{24} = 4$

For finding limiting reagent, moles of both the reactants are divided by their coefficients and the least value gives L.R.

For~${TiCl}_{4}$,~$\dfrac{1 . 88}{1} = 1 . 88$

For~$Mg$~=~$\dfrac{4}{2}= 2$

$∴$~${TiCl}_{4}$~is the limiting reagent~So, on the basis of L.R., product amount will be calculated.

$∵$~One mole of~${TiCl}_{4}$~produces one mole of~$Ti$.

~Number of moles of~$Ti$~produced by $1 . 88$ moles of~

${TiCl}_{4} = 1 . 88$~moles.

Mass of~$Ti =$~moles of~$Ti \times$~molar mass of $Ti$

$= 1 . 88 \times 48 = 90 . 24g$

$% yield = \dfrac{Experimentalyield}{Theoreticalyield} \times 100$

$= \dfrac{32}{90 \cdot 24} \times 100 ≅ 35 . 46 %$&

questions.q:
$NX$ is produced by the following step of reactions
$M + {X}_{2} \to {MX}_{2}$

$3{MX}_{2} + {X}_{2} \to {M}_{3}{X}_{8}$

${M}_{3}{X}_{8} + {N}_{2}{CO}_{3} \to NX + {CO}_{2} + {M}_{3}{O}_{4}$
How much $M$ (metal) is consumed to produce $206gm$ of $NX$.~$($Take atomic weight of $M = 56, N = 23, X = 80 )$
questions.solution:
The sequence of reactions are as follows:

$\begin{cases}M & + {X}_{2} & \to {MX}_{2} \\ {MX}_{2} & + {X}_{2} & \to {M}_{3}{X}_{8} \\ {M}_{3}{X}_{8} & + {Na}_{2}{CO}_{3} & \to NX + {CO}_{2} + {M}_{3}{O}_{4}\end{cases}$

moles of $NX = \dfrac{massofNX}{molarmassofNX} = \dfrac{206}{103} = 2mol$

$POAC$(Principle of atom conservation) for $X$ Atom :
Number~of $X$ atom in ${M}_{3}{X}_{8} =$ Number~of $X$ Atom in $NX$
$8$~[Number~of mole~${M}_{3}{X}_{8}$]~$= 1 [$ of Number~of mole of $NX ]$
Number~of moles of ${M}_{3}{X}_{8} = \left[\dfrac{2}{8}\right] = \dfrac{1}{4}$ mole


Now,~$POAC$ for $M$~Atom:

$3$~[Number~of mole of ${M}_{3}{X}_{8}$] $= 1 \times$[Number of Mole of $M$]
$3 \times \dfrac{1}{4} =$ Number~of mole of $M$

Weight of $M= molofM \times atomicmassofM = \dfrac{3}{4} \times 56 = 42gram$

questions.solution:
$\text{17}\text{.0%}$ solution of ${\text{CH}}_{3} \text{COONa}$ means that $\text{100}\text{g}$ solution contain $\text{17}\text{g}$ of ${\text{CH}}_{3} \text{COONa}$.

$\text{=}\dfrac{\text{100}\text{g}}{\text{1}\text{.09}\text{g}{\text{mol}}^{- \text{1}}} \text{=}\dfrac{\text{100}}{\text{1}\text{.09}} \text{mL}$
So molarity of solution $\text{=}\dfrac{\text{Moles}\text{of}\text{solute}}{\text{Liter}\text{of}\text{soln}\text{.}}$
$\text{=}\dfrac{\dfrac{\text{17}}{\text{82}\text{.0}} \text{mol}}{\left(\dfrac{\text{100}}{\text{1}\text{.09}}\right){\text{\times 10}}^{- \text{3}} \text{L}}$
$\text{=}\text{2}\text{.259}\text{M}\text{=}\text{2}\text{.26}\text{M}$

questions.q:
$1g$~silver salt of an organic dibasic acid on heating yields $0 . 5934gAg$. If the weight percentage of~$C$~in acid is $8$ times the weight percentage of hydrogen and one half the weight percentage of oxygen, then determine its molecular formula.

\left({M}_{AgNO3} = 108\right)$

$
questions.solution:
${RH}_{2} ⟶ {RAg}_{2} ⟶ Ag$

Apply principle of atom conservation to~$Ag$,

$\dfrac{1 . 00}{M\left({RAg}_{2}\right)} \times 2 = \dfrac{0 \cdot 534g}{108} \times 1$

$M\left({RAg}_{2}\right) = \dfrac{2 \times 108}{0 \cdot 5934} = 364g{mol}^{- 1}$

${M}_{RH2} = 364 - 216 + 2 = 150g{mol}^{- 1}$

$\begin{cases}Element & % Composition & Atomicratio & Leastratio & Leastsimpleratio \\ C & 8 & \dfrac{8}{12} = 0 . 67 & 1 . 00 & 2 . 00 \\ H & 1 & \dfrac{1}{1} = 1 . 00 & 1 . 50 & 3 . 00 \\ O & 16 & \dfrac{16}{16} = 1 . 00 & 1 . 50 & 3 . 00\end{cases}$

Empirical formula$= {C}_{2}{H}_{3}{O}_{3}$

Empirical formula mass$= 75g$per~$EFM$

$∴$~$n = \dfrac{Molecularmass}{Empiricalformula mass} = \dfrac{150}{75} = 2$

The molecular formula is ${C}_{4}{H}_{6}{O}_{6}$.

questions.q:
A 1 g sample of ${KClO}_{3}$ was heated under such conditions that a part of it decomposed according to the equation.

(i) $2{KClO}_{3} ⟶ 2KCl + 3{O}_{2}$

and the remaining underwent change according to the equation

(ii) $4{KClO}_{3} ⟶ 3{KClO}_{4} + KCl$

If the amount of ${O}_{2}$ evolved was $146 . 8mL$ at $NTP$, calculate the percentage by weight of ${KClO}_{4}$ in the residue.
questions.solution:
Apply POAC on the oxygen atoms in the equation (1)

${KClO}_{3} \to KCl + {O}_{2}$

moles of $O -$ atoms in ${KClO}_{3} =$ moles of $O -$ atoms in ${O}_{2}$ since $1$ mole of ${KClO}_{3}$ contains $3$ moles of $O -$ atoms
and $1$ mole of ${O}_{2}$ contains $2$ moles of $O -$ atoms $3x$~moles of ${KClO}_{3} = 2x$ moles of ${O}_{2}$

$3x\dfrac{wt . of{KClO}_{3}}{mol . wt . of{KClO}_{3}} = 2x\dfrac{volumeof{O}_{2}atNTP}{22400}$

wt. of~${KClO}_{3} = \dfrac{2X146 . 8X122 . 5}{3X22400} = 0 . 5358g .$

In the second reaction:

The amount of ${KClO}_{3}$ left $= 1 - 0 . 5358 = 0 . 4642g .$

${KClO}_{3} \to {KClO}_{4} + KCl$

$0 . 4642g$

Applying $POAC$ for $O -$atoms in the equation (ii),
moles of $O -$ atoms in ${KClO}_{3} =$ moles of $O -$ atoms in${KClO}_{4}$

since $1$ mole of ${KClO}_{3}$ contains $3$ moles of $O -$ atoms and $1$~mole of ${KClO}_{4}$ contains $4$ moles of $O -$ atoms $3 \times$ moles of ${KClO}_{3} = 4x$ moles of ${KClO}_{4}$

$3x\dfrac{wt . \text{of}{KClO}_{3}}{mol . wt . \text{of}{KClO}_{3}} = 4x\dfrac{wt . \text{of}{KClO}_{4}}{mol . wt . \text{of}{KClO}_{4}}$

wt. of~${KClO}_{4} = \dfrac{3x0 . 4642x138 . 5}{122 . 4x4} = 0 . 3937g .$

wt. of residue~$= 1 -$ wt. of Oxygen

$= 1 - \dfrac{146 . 8}{22400} \times 32g = 0 . 7902g$

Hence,$%$ of ${KClO}_{4}$ in the residue

$= \dfrac{0 . 3937}{0 . 7902} \times 100 = 49 . 8 %$

questions.q: An alloy of metals X and Y weighs $12g \text{ and } $ contains atoms X~and $Y$ in the ratio of $2: 5$. The percentage of Metal X in the alloy is $20$ by mass. If the atomic mass of X~is $40$ , what is the atomic mass of metal Y.
questions.solution:
According to mole concept&

Mass of metal& $X$~in alloy~$= 12 \times \dfrac{20}{100}$

Mass of metal~$Y$~in alloy~$= 12 - 2 . 4 = 9 . 6g$

Moles of~$X$~$= \dfrac{2 . 4}{40}$

Now, Number of atoms of~$X = \dfrac{2 . 4}{40} \times 6 . 023 \times {10}^{23} = 3 . 61 \times {10}^{22}$

Number of atoms of $Y = \dfrac{3 . 61 \times {10}^{22} \times 5}{2} = 9 . 025 \times {10}^{22}$

Thus, by the stoichiometry

$9 . 6gY \to 9 . 025 \times {10}^{22}atom6 . 022 \times {10}^{23} \to \dfrac{9 . 6}{9 . 025 \times {10}^{22}} \times 6 . 023 \times {10}^{23}$

Hence, the atomic mass of~$Y = 64amu$

questions.q: For a given unbalanced reaction, $\mathrm{MnO}_2+\mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{MnCl}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$, which is the limiting reagent, if the initial amount for each of the reactant is 100 grams? [Molar masses : $\mathrm{MnO}_2=86.9 ; \mathrm{HCl}=36.5$;  \left.\mathrm{MnCl}_2=125.8 ; \mathrm{Cl}_2=70.9 ; \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}=18\right]$
questions.solution:
Limiting reagent In a chemical reaction, the limiting reagent is the reactant that determine, how much of the products are made. The other reactants are sometimes referred to as being in excess, since there will be some leftover after the limiting reagent is completely used up. Given, unbalanced reaction, $\begin{array}{lcccc} & \mathrm{MnO}_2+ & \mathrm{HCl} & \longrightarrow \mathrm{MnCl}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\ \text { Initial amount } & 100 \mathrm{~g } & 100 \mathrm{~g} & & \\ \text { of reactant } & & \\ \text { Molar mass } & 86.9 & 36.5 & 125.8 & 18 \end{array} Balancing the reaction,
Convert amounts to moles Moles of \mathrm{MnO}}_{2}=100 \mathrm{~g} \times \frac{1 \mathrm{~mol}}{86.9 \mathrm{~g}}=1.15 \mathrm{~mol}$of $\mathrm{MnO}}_{2}$ Moles of \mathrm{HCl}=$100 $\mathrm{~g} \times \frac{1 \mathrm{~mol}}{36.5 \mathrm{~g}}=$2.73 $\mathrm{~mol} of $\mathrm{HCl}$ Actual ratio (molar ratio) of reactants $=$\frac{\text { Moles of } \mathrm{MnO}_2}{\text { Moles of } \mathrm{HCl}}=\frac{1.15 \mathrm{~mol}}{2.73 \mathrm{~mol}}=\frac{0.42}{1} \mathrm{~mol} The actual ratio tells us that we have 0.42 moles of \mathrm{MnO}}_{2}$ for every 1 mole of $\mathrm{HCl}$. In comparison, the stoichiometric ratio from our balanced reaction is below : $\text { Stoichiometric ratio }=\frac{1 \text { moles of } \mathrm{N}_2}{4 \text { moles of } \mathrm{HCl}}=\frac{0.25 \text { moles } \mathrm{MnO}_2}{1 \text { moles } \mathrm{HCl}}$This means we need at least 0.25 mole of $\mathrm{MnO}}_{2}$ for every mole of $\mathrm{HCl}$. Since, our actual ratio is greater then our stoichiometric ratio, we have more \mathrm{MnO}}_{2}$ than we need to react with each mole of $\mathrm{HCl}$. Therefore, $\mathrm{HCl}$ is our limiting reagent and $\mathrm{MnO}}_{2}$ is in excess. Hence, correct option is (b).

questions.q: The emperical formula of a compound is $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{O}$ and its vapour density is 45 . What is the molecular formula of the compound?
questions.solution: Given, empirical formula of compound $=\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{O}$ Vapour density $=45$ Molecular formula $=$ ? Empirical formulas show the simplest whole number ratio of atoms in a compound. Molecular formula show the number of each type of atom in a molecule. Relation between empirical formula and molecular formula. Molecular formula $=n$ (empirical formula $)n=\frac{\text { MM (molar mass) }}{\text { EFM (empirical formula molar mass) }}$ Molecular weight $=2 \times$ vapour density $=2 \times 45=90$ Let, the molecular forumula be $\mathrm{C}_{2 x} \mathrm{H}_{5 x} \mathrm{O}_x$. Therefore, $n=\frac{90 \text { (molecular weight })}{47(\text { EFM })}=1.47 \approx 2$ Value of $x=2$ Molecular formula $=\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{O}\right)_2=\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10} \mathrm{O}_2$
